findings.title: A robot bear walking in at the 3500 lock can push the hero off the right edge of the locked screen, where the hero is invisible and can't shoot, for up to 0.6 s
findings.evidence:
Cause in code. The 'block' contact push in updateEnemies has no screen clamp (src/engine.js:365-371: p.x = p.x < e.x ? tb.x - pb.w/2 : tb.x + tb.w + pb.w/2). updatePlay runs updateCamera, which clamps p.x to [cam+8, cam+W-8] (engine.js:631), BEFORE updateEnemies (engine.js:667 vs 675), so the pushed x is what gets drawn. Player bullets beyond cam+W+10 are deleted on their first update (engine.js:393). Robot bears use 'block' in walk/enter (level2_enemies.js:1119) and their box is 52 px wide (bearBox, level2_enemies.js:1120-1127). The 3500 lock sends two of them from the right edge at d260 and d760 (level2.js:95-98). They start at cam+W+40 (engine.js:650-651) and walk in at 0.7 px per frame (level2_enemies.js:980-984). A hero that is in the air at the right edge while the bear's centre passes under it lands right of the centre, is pushed to bear.x+32 (off screen), is clamped back the next frame, is still right of the centre, and is pushed out again until bear.x < cam+454.

Re-checked in this session on the fresh harness:
- fx-sandwich.js (two bears, hero holding Right): 'SANDWICH f=0 hero x=4008.6 cam=3500 screen right edge=3980 visible=false' through 'f=32 hero x=3986.2 ... visible=false', visible again at f=33 (0.55 s).
- fx-render-push.js (one wave bear; the hero holds Right at the edge and jumps 40 frames after the bear appears): 'RP f=71 hero x=4001.6 screen 3500..3980', fully off screen from frame 71 to frame 92.
- fx-push.js sweep: 'PUSH SUMMARY on foot: 13 of 60 jump timings end off screen; longest 25 frames; no jump: 0' and 'tractor: 0 of 60'.

Pictures (opened with Read): /Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work/shots/f1-sheet.png (copy of H/shots/review-fuzz/f1-sheet.png). It shows three crops, x 330-480 and y 110-250 in game pixels: frame 60, the hero jumps at the edge as the bear arrives; frame 80, the hero is gone (x 3995.3, the screen ends at 3980); frame 80 with the clamp, the hero is visible at x 3972. f1-src-f80-full.png shows the whole screen at frame 80 with no hero anywhere and the HUD still showing INES with 3 hearts.

Fuzz frequency: 289 events in 176 of 620 random-play runs. Every logged event was at cam 3500, on foot, beside a bear in state 'enter'. In campaign (b), 59 of the 120 runs that played that lock hit it; in (a), 60 of 111. Usually 1-3 times per run, 8-38 frames each. The longest, 38 frames, is the two-bear case with the hero at x 4009.3. In 2 runs the hero also ended up to 10.3 px past the left screen margin; its body was still partly visible and the cause was not traced. The plain harness bot never triggers it (0 in 90 passive runs). The push code is older than Mission 2 (backup/index-before-level2.html:1216). Mission 1's tank uses it too, but it enters at d30 of its lock and later roams no further than cam+430, so 25 Mission 1 fuzz runs (933k frames) never hit it.
findings.repro: H=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbookair-game/bf86e491-38d3-458c-a7d1-6193216e6d7e/scratchpad/harness, F=/Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work (durable copies of every fixture). Minimal, two bears: node $H/harness.mjs sim --level 2 --x 3701.6 --seed 1 --god --frames 60 --extra $F/fx-sandwich.js 2>&1 | grep SANDWICH. One bear, child-like: node $H/harness.mjs sim --level 2 --x 3701.6 --god --frames 120 --extra $F/fx-render-push.js 2>&1 | grep '^RP' (render the same with: render --frames 81 --out f80.png). Jump-timing sweep: node $H/harness.mjs sim --level 2 --x 3701.6 --seed 1 --god --frames 20000 --extra $F/fx-push.js 2>&1 | grep 'PUSH SUMMARY'. Fuzz, deterministic: node $H/harness.mjs sim --level 2 --hero 0 --seed 1 --x 3701.6 --frames 900 --extra $F/fuzz2-frozen-b.js 2>&1 | grep FUZZV gives heroOffScreen at frame 834, x 3999.5, cam 3500, near bear@3968/enter. $H/work/review-fuzz/run2.mjs gives the same line. In play: in the farm lock (camera stops at 3500), hold Right against the right edge and jump as a robot bear walks in from the right.
findings.impact: A child pressed against the right edge who jumps at an incoming bear, as the bears invite ('jump over them!'), sees the hero vanish for up to about half a second, then pop back at the edge once the bear has walked on. While out there the hero can't be seen and its shots are deleted. It does no damage and never blocks progress. It happened in about half of the random runs that played that lock.
findings.suggestion:
src/engine.js updateEnemies, 'block' branch: inside if (overlap(pb, tb) && p.y > tb.y + 8) { ... }, after the two push lines (after line 371), add:
  p.x = clamp(p.x, G.cam.x + 8, G.cam.x + W - 8); // same limits as updateCamera (engine.js:631)
This covers the on-foot and the ride branch.

Validated in this session on a patched copy, /Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work/patched/index-f1-clamp.html, which is index.html plus that one line:
- fx-push: 'on foot: 0 of 60 ... longest 0 frames' (was 13 of 60); tractor still 0 of 60.
- fx-sandwich: the hero stays visible every frame (3944.6, then 3913.7).
- harness sim, Mission 1 seeds 1-5 and Mission 2 seeds 1-5: byte-identical JSON to the unpatched index.html (e.g. Mission 1 s1: win, 8461 frames, score 14150; Mission 2 s1: win, 11234 frames, score 33000).

Side effect: at the edge the hero can stand in front of the bear's back until it walks on, which is harmless because 'block' doesn't hurt. A nicer but unvalidated alternative is to push to tb.x - pb.w/2 (the bear's front) whenever the right-hand push would leave the screen.

findings.title: bugs-1 confirmed by forced deaths at the MEGA BEAR: a hit on the last life during its 150-frame death animation, or a death that ends after the kill, gives GAME OVER and the whole orchard and boss again. bugs-1's onKill change is needed; the engine safety net alone does not fix the common cases
findings.evidence:
Campaign d2, cfg d-bossDying-l1.js: last life, hurtPlayer during the boss's 'dying' state. 8 of 8 runs went to GAME OVER, continued at 4400, and had to beat the MEGA BEAR a second time. Re-run today in the fresh harness: d-bossDying-l1 h0 s1, hero killed at frame 613 while the bear is dying, 2nd kill at 2936, win at 3294; h1 s2, death at 666, 2nd kill at 3600, win at 3963. Campaign d2, d-bossDead-b1 (hero dead on the last life once G.winT is set): 8 of 8 runs went to GAME OVER as well.

New deterministic fixture fx-bossend.js, run on three builds (output in fuzz-work/out/bugs1/bossend.txt):
- hitDuring: unpatched 'RESULT state=over at f=381 (hero died at 272)'; bugs-1 variant 'state=win at f=630 (hero died at -1, hurtPlayer calls during the death animation 150)'; safety net only 'state=over at f=381'.
- deadBefore (last heart lost 30 frames before the kill): unpatched over at 381; bugs-1 variant win at 660; safety net only over at 381.
- deadAfterWin: unpatched over at 531; bugs-1 variant win at 630; safety net only win at 630.

Regression on the bugs-1 variant: harness sims of Mission 1 seeds 1-5 and Mission 2 seeds 1-5 are byte-identical to index.html; d-bossDead-b1 wins in 4 of 4 runs with 0 game overs (about 930-963 frames); d-bossDying-l2 is unchanged (win at about 931); errors [].
findings.repro: H as in fuzz-1, F=/Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work. Boss-end check: node $H/harness.mjs sim --level 2 --x 5921.6 --seed 1 --frames 1200 [--html $F/patched/index-bugs1.html] --extra $F/cfg/be-hitDuring.js --extra $F/fx-bossend.js 2>&1 | grep '^BE'. findings.impact: As bugs-1: on the last life at the final boss, beating the MEGA BEAR can still end in GAME OVER, and continuing means the whole orchard on foot (K2) and the whole fight again.
findings.suggestion:
Apply bugs-1's suggestion in full.

level2_boss.js megabear onKill (line 1272): replace the e.pups loop with:
  for (const w of G.enemies) if (w !== e && w.active && !w.dead && !w.dying && w.state !== 'dying') damageEnemy(w, 99); const p = G.p; p.inv = Math.max(p.inv, 400); if (p.dead && G.lives <= 1) G.lives = 2;

engine.js playerRespawn (line 229): if (G.lives > 0 || G.winT > 0).

Both parts together are validated as /Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work/patched/index-bugs1.html. Do not ship the engine line alone: it only covers deaths that end after G.winT is set.

findings.title: bugs-4 confirmed as the only non-finite value anywhere in 13.9 M frames of random play: the never-drawn explosion 'flash' particles
findings.evidence: Every frame of every fuzz run checked x/y/vx/vy (and hp, inv, kb, life where present) for: the player, the camera, all enemies, player and enemy bullets, items, props, POWs, grenades and floating texts. There was 0 'nonfinite' violation in 620 runs (both missions, both heroes, all starts, the tractor, the boss, menus). The only NaN values were G.parts entries of type 'flash': 518,225 particle-frames in total, for example 141,449 in campaign (b) and 1,420-2,106 in each 40000-frame Mission 1 run. They are created without vx/vy by boom(), the same cause bugs-4 gives.
findings.repro: Any fuzz run, e.g. node /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbookair-game/bf86e491-38d3-458c-a7d1-6193216e6d7e/scratchpad/harness/work/review-fuzz/run2.mjs --level 2 --seed 1 --x 3701.6 --frames 20000 --extra /Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work/fuzz2-frozen-b.js: fuzz.stats.nanParts = {flash: N} and no 'nonfinite' entry in vCount.
findings.impact: None for play. It bounds bugs-4: nothing else in the game produces NaN or Infinity under random input.
findings.suggestion: As bugs-4: engine.js boom() pushes the flash particle with vx: 0, vy: 0, or removes it. This changes how Mission 1's explosions look (a 5-frame white flash), so it is the parent's call.

strengths:
Measured over 620 random-input runs (13.9 M frames, 64.5 h of play), plus 51 older-driver runs, 90 runs of the plain bot with the invariant checker and 237,570 frames drawn every frame. Fixes should keep all of this true:

- **No errors:** 0 thrown, console.error or swallowed (errorOnce) errors in every run, in both missions, both heroes and all starts. This includes 11,174 pauses, 72,904 Enter taps, 768 window blurs, 2,108 mute toggles, 2,827 game overs, 2,735 continues, 82 countdowns to the title, 133 new games, 119 wins and 38 ALL MISSIONS COMPLETE screens.
- **Position limits:** the camera always stayed within [0, 5720]. The hero never left the world, never went more than 1.3 px under the ground (never 3 frames in a row), and was never dead inside the tractor. There were never two tractors.
- **No stuck states:** the longest stretch without forward progress outside a busy lock was 2,003 frames (33 s, in a pause-heavy forced-death run).
- **Locks:** every camera lock finished. The 900 lock took 501-8,415 frames, 2250 took 679-16,832 and 3500 took 1,081-20,773; the long tails were god-mode personas holding Right with the last enemy behind them.
- **Bosses:** the MEGA BEAR always became hurtable after its intro (at most 214 frames; Mission 1's crab at most 260). It was killed in every god run that reached it.
- **Restarts:** the state after every continue and new game was right (lives, hearts, position, camera, checkpoint, locks, no leftovers, score, timers). 57 new games after a game-over countdown were identical to a pristine build of that mission, and the best score was saved at every countdown.
- **Bounded counts, no leaks:**
  - Peaks: enemies 31 (the level's own spawns), player bullets 20, enemy bullets 20, particles 407, items 11, fireworks 130.
  - In a 100k-frame run the heap was flat after warm-up and the caches stayed capped.
- **Tractor:** 1,831 boardings, 1,682 ↓+Z exits and 155 wrecks without a violation; it can be boarded again after every continue.
- **Intro:** it always ends under Enter spam and pause storms (hero visible, door shut, scripted keys cleared).
- **Mission 1:** 25 fuzz runs (933k frames) plus 25 plain-bot runs had no errors, no off-screen hero and no invariant violation. Bot sims are byte-identical with or without both validated patches.
coverage:
**Tools.** A random-input driver replaces the bot's keys each frame with random holds and taps of arrows, Z, X, C, ↓+Z, P/Esc, Enter, M and Space, plus window blurs and idle stretches, biased toward Right with a per-seed persona. It checks the invariants every frame and was run through the real update()/draw() with the harness boot. The scripts are durable in /Users/macbookair/game/tools/review/fuzz-work; working copies are in H/work/review-fuzz.

**Finished in earlier sessions (not redone):**
- **(a)** 120 runs from the mission start, intro included: 40 seeds × 2 heroes plus 20 × 2 in god mode, 40000 frames each.
- **(d2)** 160 forced-death runs: mid-intro, riding, boarding, each lock on the last life, the boss dying or dead, a cage burst, while paused, and death-pause storms.
- **(e)** 100 intro, menu, win and all-clear runs with Enter spam and pause storms.
- **(c)** leak runs, including a 100,000-frame god run.
- The F1 analysis.

**Finished today:**
- **(b)** complete: 9 starts (600, 1350, 2451.6, 2850, 2950, 3701.6, 4400, 5560, 5921.6) × 10 seeds × 2 heroes × 20000 frames = 180 runs, 3.6 M frames, errors [] in all. The only violation was F1, at the 3500 lock.
- **(o)** game over without continuing, then the title, then a new game: 18 distinct runs (6 from before plus 12 today), with 86 game overs, 82 countdowns that ran out (exactly 600 frames each) and 84 new games across both missions. Today's 12 add o-check.js, which compares each new game with a pristine devStart signature.
- **(df)** 7 more draw-every-frame runs (10 in total).
- Re-validated today: the F1 fix, F1's repro, and bugs-1 with its fix.

**Not findings (tool artefacts):**
- count/enemies 31: my limit of 30 was below the level's 26 spawns plus 5 lock-0 waves.
- lockTooLong: god-mode personas pinned at the right edge with the target behind them; the c leak runs had firing switched off by design.
- introKeysLeft: only after a bypass death in the intro, which hurtPlayer forbids.
- treeShake null→0: a harmless Mission 2-only field left on G in a later Mission 1 game.

**Not covered:**
- No real browser, audio, touch, gamepad or window resize.
- Frame timing: harness timing is too noisy on this loaded machine to support frame-time claims.
- Random input is not a child.
- No non-god random run beat the MEGA BEAR (60 runs from 4400 or later). Boss beatability rests on god runs and the boss's hurtable time.
- Mute only flips a flag here, and blocked localStorage was not tested.
- K2 is consistent with this data: 244 game overs in the boss-area runs restarted at 4400. K-list items are not reported again without new evidence.
